source.title: The Projection Technique for Two Open Problems of Unconstrained Optimization Problems

accepted.question_text: For unconstrained optimization of a twice continuously differentiable nonconvex function f: R^n -> R, does the Polak-Ribiere-Polyak conjugate gradient algorithm admit a globally convergent variant under the weak Wolfe-Powell line search? In the setting discussed by the source, the issue is whether one can guarantee global convergence for nonconvex objectives under that line-search regime, despite classical counterexamples showing nonconvergence for the standard PRP method.
accepted.context_brief: PRP global convergence under weak Wolfe-Powell search

evidence.quote: There are two problems for nonconvex functions under the weak Wolfe–Powell line search in unconstrained optimization problems. The first one is the global convergence of the Polak–Ribière–Polyak conjugate gradient algorithm
One open problem is the global convergence of the PRP conjugate gradient algorithm under the WWP line search for nonconvex functions
the given algorithms possess global convergence under the WWP line search and the normal conditions for nonconvex functions

accepted.question_text: For unconstrained optimization of a twice continuously differentiable nonconvex function f: R^n -> R, does the Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno quasi-Newton method admit a globally convergent variant under the weak Wolfe-Powell line search? More specifically, can one obtain global convergence for nonconvex objectives in that weak Wolfe-Powell setting even though standard BFGS is known to fail in relevant counterexamples?
accepted.context_brief: BFGS global convergence under weak Wolfe-Powell search

evidence.quote: the second is the global convergence of the Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno quasi-Newton method
The other is the global convergence of the BFGS method for nonconvex functions. It has been considered an open problem in unconstrained optimization
the other open problem is the global convergence of the BFGS quasi-Newton algorithm under the WWP line search for nonconvex functions
the given algorithms possess global convergence under the WWP line search and the normal conditions for nonconvex functions

accepted.question_text: In projection-based variants of unconstrained optimization methods that classify iterates into in-points and out-points using a boundary condition, are there boundary conditions other than the one used in this paper that can effectively separate the in-points from the out-points?
accepted.context_brief: Alternative boundary conditions for projection methods

evidence.quote: Are there other conditions such as the boundary to separate the in-points and the out-points?

accepted.question_text: For the projection framework introduced in this paper for unconstrained optimization, are there projection paraboloids better than the one studied here, in the sense of being worth further theoretical or algorithmic investigation?

evidence.quote: Are there any better projection paraboloid worth studying?
